name: handler_slowdown
title: Progression Handler: Slow Down Progress Reporting

origin.description: Delay each progress update so the steps together take about duration seconds.
origin.usage: handler_slowdown(duration = 10.0, intrusiveness = 0, target = "void", enable = getOption("progressr.enable", TRUE), ...)

arguments.name: duration
arguments.text: Total added delay in seconds. One finite number greater than or equal to 0. The default is 10.

arguments.name: intrusiveness
arguments.text: How disruptive the reporter is. The default is 0.

arguments.name: target
arguments.text: Where progress is rendered. The default is "void".

arguments.name: enable
arguments.text: If FALSE, the handler is a no-op. The default is the option progressr.enable, or TRUE when that option is unset.

origin.details: On an enabled update the handler sleeps (duration / max_steps) * amount. initiate and finish do nothing. The handler writes nothing.

translation.description: Delay each progress update so the steps together take about duration seconds.

arguments.name: duration
arguments.text: Total added delay in seconds. One finite number greater than or equal to 0. The default is 10.

arguments.name: intrusiveness
arguments.text: How disruptive the reporter is. The default is 0.

arguments.name: target
arguments.text: Where progress is rendered. The default is "void".

arguments.name: enable
arguments.text: If False, the handler is a no-op. The default is the option progressr.enable, or True when that option is unset.

translation.details: On an enabled update the handler sleeps (duration / max_steps) * amount. initiate and finish do nothing. The handler writes nothing. A duration that is not one finite number of at least 0 raises the same stopifnot message as R.
translation.example:
from progressr.evaluate import with_progress
from progressr.progressor import progressor
from progressr.reporters import handler_slowdown

handler = handler_slowdown(duration=0, enable=True)

def body():
    progress = progressor(steps=4, on_exit=False)
    total = 0
    for i in range(1, 5):
        progress()
        total += i
    return total

total = with_progress(body, handlers=handler, enable=True, interval=0, delay_terminal=False, delay_stdout=False, delay_conditions=())
print(f"handler_slowdown with duration 0 returns {total}.")
